scheme_name: National Scheme on Welfare of Fishermen
overview: The National Scheme on Welfare of Fishermen is a centrally sponsored scheme under the Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, aimed at providing financial assistance and welfare measures to fishermen and fish farmers. It supports livelihood enhancement, social security, and infrastructure development for the fisheries sector. The scheme is implemented across India and targets traditional and small-scale fishers.
objectives: Provide financial assistance for livelihood support to fishermen
Enhance social security coverage for fishers and their families
Support infrastructure development for fisheries welfare
Promote sustainable fisheries practices through welfare interventions
Strengthen institutional mechanisms for fisher welfare delivery
Facilitate access to credit and insurance for fishers
Improve living and working conditions of fisher communities
eligibility: Traditional and small-scale fishermen, fish farmers, and members of fisher communities engaged in capture fisheries, aquaculture, or allied activities, who are citizens of India and belong to economically weaker sections, as identified by State Governments/UTs based on socio-economic criteria.
benefits: Financial assistance for housing, sanitation, drinking water, community assets, and livelihood support; access to accident insurance and health coverage; support for formation of fisher cooperatives and self-help groups; skill development and training programs; and subsidies for fisheries-related equipment and infrastructure.
financial_support: The scheme provides central share of the Department of Fisheries provides financial assistance to State Governments/UTs for implementation of welfare activities for fishermen, with central share released as grants-in-aid based on approved project proposals and utilization certificates.
application_process: 1. State Governments/UTs submit project proposals for fisher welfare activities to the Department of Fisheries. 2. Proposals are appraised by the Department for technical and financial feasibility. 3. Approved projects are sanctioned with central share allocation. 4. Funds are released in installments based on utilization certificates and progress reports. 5. States implement the schemes through designated agencies and monitor outcomes.
required_documents: Bank account details of implementing agency
deadlines: Rolling basis — proposals can be submitted throughout the year as per budget cycle and scheme guidelines.
implementing_agency: Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying
caveats: Central assistance is subject to availability of funds and budget allocations
State Governments/UTs must contribute matching share as per scheme norms
Beneficiary selection must follow transparency and socio-economic criteria
Funds are released only upon submission of utilization certificates and progress reports
